cards.subject: flu
cards.heading: Flu Emergency Warning Signs in Adults
title: Flu
Warning Signs That Need the ER
cards.alt: Nine CDC emergency warning signs of flu in adults: difficulty breathing, chest or belly pain or pressure, dizziness or confusion or trouble waking, seizures, not urinating, severe muscle pain, severe weakness or unsteadiness, a fever or cough that improves then returns worse, and a chronic condition getting worse
items: Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath
Pain or pressure in the chest or belly
Fever or cough that improves, then returns

cards.subject: flu
cards.heading: The Warning Sign People Miss: Better, Then Worse
title: The
Flu
Relapse People Miss
cards.alt: The flu relapse pattern: the flu hits, the fever breaks and you feel better, then about two days later the fever and cough come back worse, which is a CDC warning sign to go to the ER

nodes.label: Go to the ER
nodes.note: A complication may have set in

cards.subject: blood pressure
cards.heading: What Blood Pressure Is Dangerously High?
title: When
Blood Pressure
Becomes a Crisis
cards.statLine: is a hypertensive crisis. Only one number has to cross the line: the top number or the bottom number.
cards.alt: A blood pressure reading of 180/120 or higher is a hypertensive crisis, and only one number has to cross the line: a top number of 180 or higher, or a bottom number of 120 or higher

cards.subject: blood pressure
cards.heading: High Reading With Symptoms: Call 911
title: High Blood Pressure Plus Any of These:
Call 911
cards.alt: Call 911 if a blood pressure reading of 180/120 or higher comes with any of these six NHLBI symptoms: a sudden severe headache, difficulty breathing, sudden severe pain in the abdomen, chest or back, numbness or weakness, a sudden change in vision, or problems talking

items.label: Severe pain
items.note: In the abdomen, chest, or back

cards.subject: vomiting
cards.heading: Vomiting: When to Go to the ER
title: When
Vomiting
Needs Care Now
cards.alt: Eight MedlinePlus signs that vomiting needs care now: blood or coffee-colored material in the vomit, suspected poisoning, vomiting longer than 24 hours, no fluids kept down for 12 hours, no urine for 8 hours, severe belly pain, a headache or stiff neck, and vomiting 3 or more times in one day
items: No fluids kept down for 12 hours
Vomited 3 or more times in 1 day

cards.subject: dehydration
cards.heading: Signs of Dehydration in Adults
title: 5 Signs of
Dehydration
in Adults
cards.alt: Five signs of dehydration in adults: less or dark yellow urine, dizziness or lightheadedness, a dry mouth and more thirst, sunken eyes, and skin that does not bounce back when pinched

items.label: Less or dark urine
items.note: Urinating less often, or dark yellow

items.label: Slow skin bounce-back
items.note: Does not bounce back when pinched
